rulingNotes.drugReason: Indications (reasons) of a patient's prescriptions, captured in the MedicationsAndTreatments scope through read plan DRUG_REASONS: a reason whose demographicNo and drug owner are both the patient. A reason on which the two disagree, or whose drug is missing, holds the drug's owner and the named patient (CDS_EXPORT_AMBIGUOUS_SOURCE). Every reason the chart shows (archivedFlag 0) travels whole in CARLOS.Medication.Reasons.v1; the indication's ICD-9 code (the one active primary reason, or the only active reason when none is primary) is ProblemCode when it fits. Archived reasons are shown nowhere in CARLOS and are accounted ARCHIVED_DRUG_REASON_NOT_SHOWN_IN_CHART. On an imported medication an original ProblemCode is kept and CARLOS reasons are added beside it.

rulingNotes.HRMDocumentComment: Comments on a selected patient's HRM reports travel whole in that report's Notes (source context), with the authors' public names; a deleted comment (deleted 1) is not shown in the chart and is accounted, not exported. An HRM report with no patient link at all is an unmatched inbox item in no chart: it holds no patient and is counted per job, never read. A report whose only links name charts that do not exist, or a row of a missing report, holds every patient.
rulingNotes.providerLabRouting: Inbox routing of lab and document reports. A route of one of a selected patient's HL7 labs (patientLabRouting of the same lab number and type) is captured in the LaboratoryResults scope; a DOC route of one of the patient's documents (its ctl_document chart link) is captured in the Reports scope as providerLabRouting_documents. An acknowledgement (status A) by a real provider is exported as ResultReviewer or ReportReviewed; a comment travels whole in the native laboratory residual record or the report Notes; new, filed, removed and unclaimed routes are operational inbox workflow. A route linked to no patient (an unmatched lab, an unfiled incoming document) is in no chart: it is counted per job, never read. A route whose link is broken holds every patient.
rulingNotes.HRMDocumentToProvider: Provider routes of a selected patient's HRM reports: a sign-off (signedOff 1) by a provider the public lookup names, with a sign-off time, is a ReportReviewed (date on the wire) and every sign-off travels whole in the report's Notes with its exact time; an unsigned route (0 or NULL) is inbox workflow; any other signedOff value holds the patient. An HRM report with no patient link at all is an unmatched inbox item in no chart: it holds no patient and is counted per job, never read. A report whose only links name charts that do not exist, or a row of a missing report, holds every patient.
rulingNotes.HRMDocumentSubClass: The accompanying subclasses CARLOS keeps for a selected patient's HRM reports travel whole in the report's Notes; the active one is the SubClass when the message states none, and they are the OBRContent of a report whose message file cannot be read. An HRM report with no patient link at all is an unmatched inbox item in no chart: it holds no patient and is counted per job, never read. rulingNotes.HRMDocument: Every Hospital Report Manager report linked to a selected patient (an HRMDocumentToDemographic row of the patient, as the inbox scope links it) is exported as one CDS 5.2 Reports entry in the Reports scope (read plan HRM_REPORTS): the stored message file (hrm_report_files) is read as the report viewer reads it and gives Media, Format, the content (TextContent, or the decoded binary attached at FilePath), Class, SubClass, EventDateTime, ReceivedDateTime, SourceAuthorPhysician, SendingFacilityId, SendingFacilityReport, OBRContent, HRMResultStatus, MessageUniqueID and RecipientName; sourceFacility is SourceFacility; the rest of the row is the report's source context in Notes, except the duplicate-detection digests and the storage location (operational). A report whose file cannot be read (none recorded, missing, an unsupported name) is exported from these recorded details; a stored file that is not a readable HRM message is attached as stored. A message with more than one report holds the patient. An HRM report with no patient link at all is an unmatched inbox item in no chart: it holds no patient and is counted per job, never read. A report whose only links name charts that do not exist, or a row of a missing report, holds every patient.

The note itself is exported once, as the chart shows it, in its own ClinicalNotes or CPP occurrence under its per-note authorization; every link row of every revision travels exactly in that occurrence's source context (the note details of a ClinicalNotes entry, which also opens with a statement naming the records, or the CARLOS.NativeHistory.v1 residual of a CPP item). rulingNotes.GroupNoteLink: Operational, rule GROUP_NOTE_RECIPIENT_LINK: a CAISI group note is written in one chart (casemgmt_note.demographic_no) and shown read-only in each recipient chart this row names (GroupNoteAction, GroupNoteSelect2Action; CaseManagementView2Action shows it only in a facility with group notes enabled and to a provider holding the note's reporter role). The row carries only that linkage: note id, recipient, created time, whether the recipient is an anonymous client generated for the session and whether the share is still active. The note itself is exported once, with the chart that wrote it, under its per-note authorization. Copying it into a recipient's package would disclose a note of another chart (group notes commonly name the other members) without that chart's authorization, and a data summary of the row would show only another chart's note number. No longer holds the recipient chart.
